item.title: Her 911 Call Could Have Saved Denise Amber Lee
item.description: In 2008, Denise Amber Lee was abducted from her Florida home and managed to call 911 from her captor’s phone, pleading to see her family again. Despite her call and a witness reporting the abduction, police failed to reach her before she was murdered.

item.title: The Baby’s Death Changed New Mexico Law
item.description: Five-month-old Brianna Lopez died in 2002 after months of abuse by members of her family. Her mother, father and uncle were convicted, and the case helped prompt New Mexico to strengthen penalties for child abuse resulting in death through legislation later known as Brianna’s Law.

item.title: Her Husband Hired A Man To Kill Her
item.description: Kelley Clayton was killed in her New York home in 2015 by Michael Beard, a former employee of her husband Thomas. Prosecutors argued Thomas arranged the murder and created an alibi at a poker game. He was convicted of murder and sentenced to life in prison.

item.title: Ed Gein’s Grave Became A True Crime Attraction
item.description: After Ed Gein died in a Wisconsin psychiatric hospital in 1984, his grave became a target for souvenir hunters and true crime enthusiasts. His gravestone was repeatedly vandalized before being stolen in 2000 and later recovered, leaving his burial site unmarked.
